definition: Rewriting text to change its style — formality, sentiment, politeness — while preserving content.
details: Rewriting text to change its style — formality, sentiment, politeness — while preserving content. Approaches use style-conditioned generation or disentangled representations.

explainer.lead: Text style transfer rewrites text to change its style — formality, sentiment or politeness — while preserving its content. It matters because it lets one message be recast for different audiences without rewriting from scratch.

tiers.eli5: It is like saying the same thing again in a different tone of voice, keeping the message but changing how it sounds.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use style-conditioned generation or disentangled representations to separate content from style. The pitfall is preserving content exactly while the style changes, since the two are entangled in natural text and drift easily.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the task maps an input text with style s to an output with style s' such that content is preserved, approached via style-conditioned generation or disentangled representations. The known limit is the difficulty of guaranteeing content preservation when style and content are not cleanly separable.

explainer.example: Turning a blunt message into a polite one, or a formal report sentence into a casual one, without altering the underlying request.
